newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay Pacific February FTKS up 17.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Cathay Pacific February FTKS up 17.6 pct.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd reported a 17.6 percent rise in freight tonne kilometres(FTKs) and a 14.6 percent increase in the amount of cargo carried during February compared with the same month last year, airline statistics showed.
FTKs are derived by multiplying the weight of cargo by the distance flown.
Cargo load factor was also up 6.9 percent and the available cargo tonne-kms total increased 5.3 percent. The available tonne kilometre total rose 7.4 percent.
Cathay Pacific Cargo's marketing and sales manager, Ray Jewell said he was "very pleased."

"The market is quite strong on most of our major routes and it's been quite healthy for the first part of the year. Over the last year we have had quite healthy growth and the markets are performing very well. We're cautiously optimistic for the rest of the year," Jewell said.

"We are entering a period when the market is traditonally slack on a yearly basis and we will see how perform then, but because of the performance shown so far we're hoping demand will stay pretty good right through the slack," Jewell added.

Cathay reported a slight rise in the amount of passengers carried during February, up 0.3 percent to 885,086. Passenger load factor was 2.4 percent up with a 9.3 percent rise in available seat-kms and a 13.0 percent rise in revenue-passenger-kms.
During January, Cathay reported an 18.5 percent rise in the amount of cargo carried along with a 22 percent rise in freight tonne-km and a 7.2 percent increase in cargo load factor.
